intake: spiritual-unaffiliated: panpsychist-leaning with a Buddhist tilt; no personal God, but I think experience is built into matter rather than produced by it, and I meditate more than I pray.

walk.note: Descriptively true of me; I was given the stories before I could ask for them.
If the texts are human, you look at the world instead; fair enough.
The first-cause point lands; the hides-or-can't-be-seen dilemma assumes God is an object that could be visible, which classical theism never claimed, but I end up doubting anyway.
One prayer study only kills the intervening God, and move 3 had already left that God behind, but disbelief in the account is where I am.
Mind not reducing to matter gives you non-reduction, not two substances; panpsychism and neutral monism are sitting right there and get skipped.
Brain-dependence and the interaction problem sink substance dualism, but they show mind depends on the brain, not that mind is just something matter does; the hard problem is untouched.
Yes, 'matter' is a nineteenth-century word; fields and energy are what a chemist actually works with.
Structure versus what has the structure is exactly the Russellian point; I'd call the destination panpsychism rather than dream, but 'reality is at bottom experience' is my view.

'The brain is the only structure known to create consciousness' is false by my lights (it's the only structure known to report it), and it contradicts the Dream position you just reached, where you no longer need a brain to have experience.
Granting Subject, Strawson's point carries; I'd just extend 'subjects' well past things with brains.
It's a choice and I'd make the same one; compassion under uncertainty is the Buddhist move too.
Care ahead of proof does teach you where your knowledge stops; the entropy paragraph is noise.
You list equanimity as an open response and I'd pick it; and the non-fungibility premise assumes a persisting self is what carries the good, which I don't grant.
Religion₂'s hope was toward the good continuing through mercy, not toward a maker, and the move itself concedes being a maker doesn't make you resolved.
A bargain with whom, over what? There is no content here to take or refuse.
The move admits Aquinas's non-discursive knowing hasn't been shown incoherent, so the conclusion isn't earned; and as a meditator I'd also dispute that to think is always to ignore.
Value located in beings is the right place to put it; I'd put it in more beings than you would.
You say yourself the need to be remembered is a motive, not evidence; a motive for asking a question doesn't carry you to a position.
Waiting for data assumes the outside could in principle prove the inside; your own move 8 says structure never gives you what has the structure, so there is no data to wait for.

first_exit.why: I agree with the premise that mind does not seem to reduce to matter, but the only options on the table are 'two kinds of thing' or 'only matter'. The monist position that fits the premise, experience as an intrinsic aspect of what physics describes, is never offered, so the step to dualism is a false choice.

comment: Your own premises at moves 5 and 8 (mind doesn't reduce, physics gives structure but not what has it) point straight at panpsychism or Russellian monism, and the map never names it, so you bounce between dualism and materialism when the position that reconciles them is missing. The second turn leans almost entirely on one unargued premise, that subjective good requires the persistence of a particular self, and a Buddhist-leaning reader just doesn't grant it. And the question you paused on at move 19 is one you already answered at move 8: the outside cannot prove the inside, so no future system will supply the data you are waiting for.
